data.title: BHEL bags ₹600-900 crore order from Power Grid for Barmer project
data.description:
Bharat Heavy Electricals(BHEL) has received an order worth ₹600 crore to ₹900 crore from Power Grid Corporation of India for setting up synchronous condensers at the Barmer-II HVDC Terminal Station in Rajasthan.

In a regulatory filing dated November 7, BHEL said it had received a Notification of Award (NOA) from Power Grid, acting on behalf of its project special purpose vehicle (SPV), for the establishment of two synchronous condenser units with a capacity of +300/-200 MVAR each.

The project is valued at ₹600 crore to ₹900 crore, excluding Goods and Services Tax (GST).

Under the contract, BHEL will undertake the design, engineering, manufacturing, supply, erection, testing and commissioning of the two synchronous condenser units at the Barmer-II HVDC Terminal Station.

The company has been given 44 months to execute the order. BHEL classified the contract as a domestic order.

The filing also clarified that the promoters or promoter group companies have no interest in the entity awarding the contract. The order does not fall under related-party transactions.

What are synchronous condensers?

Synchronous condensers are rotating electrical machines used to support power system stability. They help manage reactive power, regulate voltage and improve the reliability of electricity transmission networks.

These systems are particularly relevant to high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission infrastructure, where voltage control and grid stability are important for reliable power transmission.

The Barmer-II HVDC Terminal Station is the location identified for the installation of the two units under the latest contract.BHEL share price

Shares of BHEL closed at ₹416 on the BSE on Friday, November 7, down ₹1.75 or 0.42% from the previous close. The stock opened at ₹416 during the session and has a 52-week high of ₹463.60 and a 52-week low of ₹239.25.

BHEL is a government-owned engineering and manufacturing company operating in the power and industrial equipment sectors. Its operations include the manufacture and supply of equipment and execution of projects across the power generation and transmission value chain.

data.title: Malaysia's king warns against challenging his order allowing house arrest for ex-PM Najib
data.description:
Key points:
  • Royal pardon lets Najib serve remaining two years at home after 50 million ringgit fine was paid
  • Najib faces separate 15-year sentence linked to 1MDB case
  • Attorney-general's office wants clarity over court order's effect on Najib's sentences
  • A-G seeking audience with king to explain legal issues, does not intend to disregard royal pardon

Malaysia's king warned on Saturday that any attempt to challenge his order letting former Prime Minister Najib Razak move from jail to house arrest could amount to defying his decree, a day after authorities delayed Najib's transfer.

Najib has been in jail since 2022 after being found guilty of corruption and money laundering in a case linked to a multibillion-dollar scandal at state fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB). He has consistently denied wrongdoing.

He was due to be transferred home on Friday, after his party paid a 50-million-ringgit ($12-million) fine to fulfil a condition of a royal pardon issued by King Sultan Ibrahim in September that would allow him to serve his remaining two years at home.

However, the attorney-general's office suspended the transfer after it said questions had arisen over the legal interpretation of the royal pardon and a court order issued on Friday allowing Najib to leave jail.

PARDON ORDER WAS CLEAR, KING SAYS

Sultan Ibrahim said on Saturday his pardon order was "clear, explicit and without any ambiguity." He also said that the attorney-general and federal territories minister had attended the pardons board meeting after which the order was issued.

"There should therefore be no confusion over its interpretation, nor should there be prolonged uncertainty over the implementation of the decision that has been granted," the king said in a statement issued by the national palace.

The house arrest order applies only to Najib's first conviction.

He faces an additional 15 years in prison after being found guilty last year in another 1MDB-linked case, with the sentence set to begin after his stint in house arrest ends. Najib is appealing the verdict.

The attorney-general sought on Saturday an audience with the king to apologise and explain the legal questions arising from Friday's court order, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's office said in a statement.

The Attorney-General's Chambers had earlier rejected accusations by Najib's lawyers of executive overreach, saying it did not intend to disregard the king's pardon but wanted the court to clarify the order's effect on Najib's sentences.

The king, a position held in rotation by Malaysia's nine regional sultans, plays a largely ceremonial role but ​has the authority to grant pardons, under discretionary powers granted by the constitution.

Malaysians hold the monarch and the country's other sultans in deep respect. Negative remarks about the royalty can be prosecuted under the colonial-era Sedition Act.

($1 = 4.0560 ringgit)

data.title: Ex-Congressman Patrick McHenry Admits He ‘Made A Mistake’ By Splitting Stablecoin Bill From CLARITY Act
data.description:
Key points:
  • McHenry said that the market structure bill split had looked good earlier.
  • According to him, the end Democrats had walked away from an excellent deal.
  • McHenry was also skeptical of Rep. Maxine Waters, a Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee.

Former Republican congressman Patrick McHenry, who chaired the House Financial Services Committee, said on Friday that he "made a mistake" by splitting stablecoin rules from the broader crypto market-structure bill.

Speaking with journalist Eleanor Terrett, McHenry admitted that decision helped derail the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (CLARITY Act), and traced the trouble back to his own time as chair.

"I do have ownership in that too, and I made a mistake, and that mistake did impair us getting a market structure bill done, and that was when I separated stablecoins, and a market structure bill, and I made that decision that we're going to have two pieces of legislation," he said.

He added that the split looked like the smarter path at the time. "It didn't have to be that way. It neatly divided that way, and I thought it was the right thing to do at the time because I thought we had a better shot of bipartisan legislation on stablecoins. I was wrong," he said.

McHenry said the stablecoin bill, the GENIUS Act, moved quickly once it stood alone, and that took pressure off market structure. The Clarity Act then hit a wall in the Senate in September, when a procedural vote to take it up fell short of the 60 votes needed.

Blame Spreads To Senate

McHenry said his decision was only one part of the failure. He also pointed to the Senate's slow committee process and the approaching midterm campaign. "And then you got to the summer, and Schumer strategically slow-rolled the process, which brought it to September. And I think that was a political move for his members and the Senate political map," he said.

By then, he said, the politics had hardened. "I think what happened was in the end Democrats walked away from an excellent deal, an excellent compromise, and they simply refused because you're in the political cycle," he said.

He also faulted the industry for waiting too long. "So take something good rather than holding out for something great. And I think a deal made at the beginning of the year was better than a deal that could be made in summer or the fall," he said. Asked whether the industry was trying to avoid a bad law, he said, "Well, the justification is always you don't want bad law, but perfection became the key here."

Regulators To Fill Gap

With legislation stalled, McHenry said crypto rules would now come from regulators. "Though we're not getting clarity in law, we're going to get something close to it through regulation," he told Terrett. He warned that those gains could be reversed if the industry stepped back. "If we're engaged, if we pull back, if crypto pulls back, they can roll back those policies very readily without consequence. So we need to stay at it," he said.

McHenry was also skeptical of Rep. Maxine Waters (D-CA), a Democrat on the House Financial Services Committee. Terrett said Waters had called for "tough but fair" crypto rules in a memo on Friday. McHenry said, "It means very bad law. It would be a very bad piece of legislation that she would craft on crypto market structure."

He said the industry still had enough support in both parties to block harmful bills. "They will not be able to pass anti-crypto laws though because we built inroads in both parties on crypto," he said.

Crypto Coalition That Blew It

McHenry made similar points earlier in the day in an interview with Bloomberg Television. Asked whether a deal was possible in the incoming Congress, he said, "Not after the election results we just saw." He put much of the blame on the industry. "Frankly, you had a crypto coalition that blew it. They had an opportunity to legislate, and they were holding out for something that was unattainable, a perfect piece of legislation," he said. "Rather than take something that was good, many of them held out for perfection, and now have ended up with nothing legislatively."

He also pointed to the GENIUS Act and stablecoin use as where adoption was already happening, while he said the rest of crypto’s integration into traditional finance would be delayed without a market-structure law. That puts stablecoin issuers like Circle Internet Group (CRCL), which issues the USDC stablecoin, a step ahead of the rest of the industry.

CRCL stock closed down over 2% on Friday. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around CRCL remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

data.title: She Was Told 'This Is Your Job.' The Invisible Caregiving Crisis Draining Savings. — Barrons.com
data.description:
People in their 50s who end up leaving work to care for their parents often have a hard time saving enough for retirement.

By Debbie Carlson

Helping out mom and dad in their twilight years is a financial struggle for people in their 40s. It is even worse for people in their 50s.

Lory Frenkel, 50, of New Brunswick, N.J., knows full well. She began taking care of her mom a decade ago when she was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. When mom died in 2021, her dad, Larry Frenkel, now 82, began having his own health issues, including having back surgery, and breaking bones three times. He now has dementia.

As her father's health has worsened, Frenkel has had to do more and more to take care of him. "My dad's needs at this point require a lot of flexibility on my part, which is not really compatible with full-time work," she says.

Frenkel pieces together freelance editing jobs, working when her father is sleeping or during the two days when he is in adult daycare. She also uses his time in daycare to fit in errands and other tasks since he can't be left unsupervised. In 2025, Lory Frenkel was laid off from her full-time job as an editor and estimates she now makes about 25% of that six-figure salary.

Between her dad's pension and her slim earnings, the family just makes ends meet to cover basic expenses and the home mortgage, including the $100 a day for Larry Frenkel's daycare. There's no money left over for savings and Frenkel can't focus on her own future.

Old 401(k) accounts are sitting at previous employers that she should consolidate. Even worse, she isn't earning enough for her to contribute additional money to her retirement accounts. "It suddenly occurred to me I really should be paying more attention to that now," she says. "But I'm so consumed with not just managing all my dad's health problems, but managing all of his finances."

Many people view their 50s as their best chance to ramp up savings for retirement since traditionally the big-ticket expenses of kids' education or house purchases are often easing, freeing up money. It is often when people hit their peak earnings as well.

Ending up as a caregiver can waylay their plans to turbocharge their savings. A 2025 Allianz Life Annual Retirement Survey of Millennial and Gen X respondents showed 60% of people surveyed who are caring for older parents didn't expect or planned to support their parents by the time they reached their 50s. An August survey by the Pew Research Center showed 45% of those in their 50s surveyed were caring for a living parent over age 65 versus 36% in 2021, the last time Pew conducted this research.

The financial hit can be serious even if caregiving is only short lived. Kimberly Zimmerman Rand, a Boston-based financial planner, says she took off about three months from work this year after her mom, Carol Zimmerman, 82, fell twice in early 2026 at her home in Rhode Island.

At first Rand traveled between suburban Boston and Rhode Island nearly daily when her mom was in a rehabilitation center after fracturing her back. When her mother broke her hip during a second fall, Rand transferred her mom to Boston, which included another round of hospitalization and multiple rehab facilities.

Missing three months of work likely cost Rand about $25,000 in lost business. "As a self-employed person, you're thinking about seeking out projects, cultivating new customers. I think I'm going to feel this into next year," she says.

Medicare covered most of her mom's urgent medical needs, but Rand was forced to pay for rehab that was recommended but deemed not medically required. For two rehab centers in Rhode Island where her mom had physical and occupational therapy, Rand paid $400 a day out of pocket for a total of about four weeks. In suburban Boston, she paid more than $600 a day for three days of extra rehab while Rand and her husband scrambled to figure out a suitable place for Carol when the center was ready to send her into Rand's care after Medicare stopped paying.

Twice Rand appealed to Medicare for additional care when she thought her mother was too fragile to be discharged from rehab, but both were denied.

Rand and her husband moved her mom from the last rehab center directly to an independent-living retirement community in Rhode Island, even though they weren't sure her mom was fully ready. Her mom has mostly recovered from her injuries, and the community has assisted living and memory care if she needs it.

Rand calls herself "a little naive" in what she expected the healthcare system to do when it came to her mom's care and how much medical professionals expected adult children to taken on these roles. Rand, who also has two college-aged teenagers, says she was shocked at the expectation she would pause her work and family responsibility to fill in caregiving gaps.

"(There was) the assumption that the adult daughter was going to stop everything and do whatever healthcare wasn't going to take care of...From the beginning to the end of that three-month period, most people would say, 'No, no, no, this is actually your job,'" she says. That was despite having no training in caregiving and not having a home suitable to accommodate a convalescing patient.

As a financial planner, Rand coaches clients to talk to their parents in advance about what happens when their health declines. But Rand found her own mother refused to have that conversation with her.

"In the back of my mind, I knew a crisis was going to precipitate all of these changes, and it did," she says.

She still recommends having the conversations, but also acknowledging that your parents won't want to do it. "Plan B (is) start figuring out how you're going to do this without the plan," she says.

Write to editors@barrons.com

data.title: After midterm rout, Vance tries to build his own 2028 brand
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump's sagging popularity weighed on Republican candidates in Tuesday's election losses
  • Vice President Vance centered closing pitch on his own agenda, not Trump's record
  • Vance remains a likely 2028 frontrunner despite lacking Trump's nationwide political machinery

By Jacob Bogage

Late in his blitz to salvage Republicans' midterm fortunes, Vice President JD Vance shifted strategy. He talked less about President Donald Trump and more about the issues that define his own political identity.

Vance argued the case for Republicans, who lost control of Congress in Tuesday’s vote, almost exclusively through the lens of his policy portfolio, according to a Reuters review of half a dozen speeches since the Republican convention in September.

He bypassed Trump's signature policies including the Iran war and deportations as polls showed the president's sagging popularity dragging down Republican office-seekers.

The change was deliberate, according to two people familiar with the strategy. Vance and his advisers saw the issues he championed — economic nationalism, foreign policy restraint, and public safety — as politically potent subjects he could address with authority. While Trump embraced them as part of his MAGA movement, Vance had emerged as their lead crusader, the people said.

The shift offered an early glimpse of how the 42-year-old vice president could chart his own course as Republicans begin looking beyond Trump.

Vance hasn’t said whether he will run for president in 2028, and Trump hasn’t endorsed him or anyone else. But Vance is viewed as a leading potential contender who some Republican officials say will need to inherit much of Trump’s coalition while separating himself from his boss's baggage.

Vance took a more public step on Wednesday toward reinforcing his own political brand with an unusually blunt election postmortem. In a social media post, he blamed the Iran war for Republicans’ midterm defeat and laid out a platform for a Republican rebound.

He called for a swift end to the conflict and urged Republicans to focus on affordability, reevaluate foreign relations and overhaul the US relationship with Israel.

Trump has called Americans’ affordability concerns a Democratic “hoax.” He launched a war against Iran following sustained lobbying from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Trump went on to endorse Netanyahu in the Israeli election.

VANCE MAKES UNEASE AT THE WAR PUBLIC

The post for the first time put Vance openly on the side of ending the war.

Three people familiar with the White House and Vance's communications told Reuters that the vice president was not breaking with Trump and said White House chief of staff Susie Wiles knew in advance about Vance's post.

On Friday, Trump reshuffled senior White House leadership, replacing Wiles with Stephen Miller in a move that suggests the White House plans to double down on some of Trump’s more hardline policies.

Trump has acknowledged the Iran war played a role in the Republican rout because of the resulting high gas prices but has continued to defend it. "I would have done nothing different," he told reporters on Wednesday.

Reuters could not determine whether Trump was aware of the post in advance.

Donald Trump Jr., the president's eldest son, endorsed Vance's remarks on social media, along with some conservative allies.

The dialogue further elevated Vance as a potential post-Trump conservative standard-bearer, said Michael Ricci, a Republican strategist and former adviser to House Speakers John Boehner and Paul Ryan.

USING THE MEGAPHONE OF THE VICE PRESIDENCY

He said Vance’s message forced conservatives to debate the merits of the war, and more broadly, what core tenets Republican presidential candidates should embrace in 2028.

"It’s simplistic to say this about him looking for ways to differentiate himself from Trump," Ricci said. "This is about him using his megaphone of the vice presidency to set the terms of debate."

Representatives for Vance declined to comment. White House representatives referred Reuters to Trump's comments on Wednesday, when he told reporters he understood Vance's perspective on the election results.

Democrats are poised to tie Vance – or any Republican nominee – to Trump in 2028, especially if Trump plays a large role in vetting conservative hopefuls.

"There’s a real challenge of how you position yourself to be viable in a general election while winning a primary that still requires you to bow down and kiss the ring,” said Igor Volsky, a Democratic strategist.

Vance’s brand did not emerge from the midterms unscathed. Republicans lost in states where he campaigned. Some of the strategies he endorsed – including an ad by Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy that cast doubt on the sexual abuse suffered by the victorious Democratic candidate, Amy Acton – may have swung races away from Republicans.

Other possible 2028 presidential contenders have offered their diagnoses of the midterm defeat. US Senator Ted Cruz of Texas said Republicans hadn't done enough on affordability. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said losing candidates had focused too heavily on transgender issues and neglected voter concerns about data centers and artificial intelligence. Secretary of State Marco Rubio has stayed silent.

Vance's effort to shape the debate was visible during the closing days of the campaign.

In stump speeches, he told voters to support Republicans because they would investigate fraud in federal health care and antipoverty programs, tying that to the White House's immigration agenda and cost of living. He almost entirely ignored the Iran war and gas prices, and seldom mentioned Trump by name.

“I want my kids to raise a family in a country that is vibrant and thriving and free and prosperous. I want the simple things,” Vance told one of his final rallies in North Carolina. “And because I want that for me, I want it for you too.”

data.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s Alleged Chinese Spy Connection Was Flagged Before Trump’s Xi Summit: Report
data.description:
Key points:
  • The memo, based on information obtained by American intelligence, reportedly said Huang had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia.
  • The U.S. intelligence community believes Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main civilian intelligence agency, according to people familiar with the memo.
  • The document was shared with a small group of senior U.S. government officials ahead of Trump's China visit.

Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang is facing fresh scrutiny over his China connections after U.S. intelligence reportedly flagged an alleged romantic relationship between the chip executive and a woman believed to have been recruited as a Chinese spy.

U.S. officials prepared a memo detailing the alleged relationship earlier this year, shortly before President Donald Trump traveled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, according to a report by The Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia shares gained nearly 3% in Friday’s regular trading, and rose another 1% during the afterhours session.

US Intelligence Believes Chinese Executive Was Recruited As Spy, Says Report

The memo, based on information obtained by American intelligence, reportedly said Huang had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer of Nvidia.

The U.S. intelligence community believes Alice Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main civilian intelligence agency, according to people familiar with the memo.

The document was shared with a small group of senior U.S. government officials ahead of Trump's China visit. The chipmaker has previously said Huang meets "thousands of customer executives every year."

Photographs and videos showing Huang with the Megaspeed executive have also circulated on social media. Alice Huang could not be reached for comment.

The allegations add another layer to Washington's scrutiny of Megaspeed, which has faced U.S. investigations over claims that it smuggled advanced Nvidia chips into China in violation of American export controls.

Megaspeed was spun off from a Chinese gaming company in 2023. Nvidia previously conducted an internal investigation into the alleged smuggling activity but concluded there was no evidence of wrongdoing.

Republican Lawmakers Seek Answers From Huang Over China Ties

The revelations come a day after senior Republican lawmakers asked Huang to appear privately before the House China, foreign affairs and intelligence committees.

The lawmakers want to question the Nvidia CEO about a New York Times report that U.S. intelligence had concluded he was the target of a Chinese spying operation. They also want answers about the company's security protocols.

Washington's concerns come amid intensifying competition with Beijing over artificial intelligence and advanced semiconductors. U.S. officials fear that China's access to cutting-edge chips could accelerate its military modernization.

Huang has also drawn criticism from national security officials for personally lobbying Trump earlier this year to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to Chinese customers.

The Nvidia CEO has maintained a close relationship with Trump, holding multiple meetings with the president since he began his second term in 2025.

Huang was initially left off the list of executives traveling with Trump to China in May. After learning of the omission, Trump reportedly called Huang, who subsequently flew to Alaska to board Air Force One during its stopover.

Huang later attended the state dinner Trump hosted for Xi during the Chinese president's September visit to the U.S.

What Retail Investors Think Of NVDA Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Nvidia trended in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Diwali Rally Lifts Sensex 8.82%, Nifty 8.58% In Best Weekly Gain Since 2021
data.description:
Benchmark indices extended their seven-session winning streak as overseas investors returned and oil prices recorded their steepest weekly decline since 2020

Indian equity markets recorded their strongest weekly gains in nearly six years, as a combination of foreign investor buying, falling crude oil prices and improving global sentiment fuelled a broad rally on Dalal Street. The gains extended the benchmark indices’ winning streak to seven consecutive sessions on Friday, with banking stocks leading the advance.

The Nifty 50 climbed 8.58 per cent during the week, while the BSE Sensex advanced 8.82 per cent, marking their biggest weekly gains since February 2021. The rally pushed the Nifty above the 25,000 mark for the first time in the period, while the Sensex closed above 81,000.

The Nifty settled at 25,030.35 on Friday, gaining 2 per cent from the previous session. The Sensex rose 2.17 per cent to close at 81,028.02. Both indices are now close to their levels before the West Asia conflict began on 28 February.

Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) bought a record Rs 45,960 crore worth of Indian equities during the week, providing substantial support to domestic markets. In contrast, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) recorded their largest-ever weekly net selling of Rs 24,197 crore.

On Friday alone, FPIs purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore, while DIIs sold shares worth Rs 5,968.7 crore. The foreign buying came amid a sharp selloff in global artificial intelligence stocks, encouraging investors to explore opportunities in other markets.

The financial services segment emerged as one of the strongest performers during the week. The Nifty Financial Services index gained 10.41 per cent, reflecting the strength of private-sector banking stocks.

Mahindra and Mahindra led the Nifty 50 gainers on Friday, rising 5.11 per cent, followed by ICICI Bank, which advanced 4.75 per cent to Rs 1,571.20. However, the rally remained concentrated in large-cap stocks, with the Nifty Midcap 150 declining 0.09 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap 250 falling 0.85 per cent.

Market Capitalisation Surges

The scale of the recovery was also visible in the market capitalisation of benchmark companies. Between 30 October and 6 November, the combined market value of Nifty 50 constituents increased by Rs 14.83 trillion to Rs 200.81 trillion, representing a rise of around 8 per cent.

Private-sector banks contributed Rs 3.23 trillion, accounting for 22 per cent of the total increase. The Nifty gained 1,977.25 points over seven trading sessions, compared with an advance of just 432 points during the entire month of October.

Data from the derivatives market also indicated that short-covering contributed to the rally. Nifty futures rose 8.4 per cent during the week, while open interest declined 17.6 per cent. The combination of rising prices and falling open interest generally indicates that traders are closing existing short positions.

FPIs also closed 103,315 Nifty 50 futures contracts during the week, suggesting that investors were reducing bearish positions previously built to hedge their cash-market exposure.

Rupee Strengthens Further

The equity market rally coincided with a sharp recovery in the domestic currency. The rupee appreciated 0.60 per cent against the US dollar on Friday to close at 93.91, its strongest level since 22 April, 2026.

The currency opened at 94.49 against the previous close of 94.47 and touched an intraday high of 93.83 before surrendering some gains. Friday's appreciation was its biggest single-day rise since 12 October, when it strengthened 0.99 per cent.

The rupee has now gained for six consecutive sessions and emerged as Asia's best-performing currency in November, following its second position in October after the South Korean won. Lower crude oil prices and increased foreign investment in domestic equities supported the recovery.

In the near term, spot USD/INR is expected to move lower, with support at 93.50 and resistance at 94.30, according to the market outlook cited in the information.

The improvement in the currency came despite continued pressure on India's foreign exchange reserves. The country's reserves declined by USD 2.7 billion to USD 717.06 billion in the week ended October 30, marking their eighth consecutive weekly fall.

Foreign currency assets declined by USD 2.09 billion, while gold reserves fell by USD 559 million. From their record high of USD 785.7 billion in the week ended 4 September, reserves have dropped by USD 68.7 billion over eight weeks, as the Reserve Bank of India sold dollars to contain volatility in the foreign exchange market.

Crude Prices Ease Pressure

The decline in international crude oil prices provided another major support to Indian financial markets. Brent crude recorded its biggest weekly percentage decline since the Covid-triggered market crash in 2020, falling nearly 18 per cent from its October 30 high of USD 117.64 a barrel.

The January 2027 Brent contract declined to USD 96.84 a barrel on Friday, compared with USD 98.29 in the previous session. Spot crude prices also eased to USD 96.07 a barrel from USD 98.69 on Thursday. Brent was trading at USD 98.26 a barrel at 6.15 pm IST on Friday.

The decline followed reports of diplomatic engagement between the US and Iran, alongside the performance of the Democratic Party in the US midterm elections. Losses for President Donald Trump's Republican Party have raised expectations of a possible de-escalation in the conflict involving the US, Israel and Iran.

For India, lower crude prices could reduce the oil import bill, ease inflationary pressures and improve the financial position of state-run oil marketing companies (OMCs).

India imported around 122 million tonnes of crude oil during the first half of FY27, broadly unchanged from the corresponding period a year earlier. However, the value of these imports increased 47 per cent to USD 90.6 billion.

The US election outcome could also reduce uncertainty surrounding trade policy. Democrats are generally viewed as less supportive of reciprocal tariffs, potentially lowering the risk of US action against India's purchases of Russian crude.

Oil Marketing Companies Face Challenges

Despite the recent decline in crude prices, the operating environment for OMCs remains challenging. Even when crude traded around USD 94 a barrel earlier in the week, prices were not particularly favourable for their marketing margins. Brent's subsequent recovery above USD 98 has added to the pressure, while domestic retail fuel prices remain capped.

Oil companies are already absorbing substantial under-recoveries on petrol, diesel and LPG. A sustained decline in international prices could provide some relief, while a reduction in geopolitical tensions may allow India to increase crude imports from West Asia because of the region's geographical proximity.

However, the outlook remains uncertain as geopolitical developments continue to influence supply expectations. Crude prices had remained elevated even when diplomatic negotiations between the US and Iran failed to make progress, despite most oil shipments continuing to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.

Renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure have added another layer of uncertainty to the market. Even if the conflict subsides, crude prices may not necessarily remain low. Strategic reserves held by several global companies have declined, and efforts to replenish inventories could generate additional demand for West Asian supplies, potentially keeping international oil prices elevated.

data.title: They Can Barely Drive, but They're Flying Planes: The Surprising Rise of Teen Pilots — WSJ
data.description:
By Allison Pohle and Alison Sider

At 17, Parker Allen was training for his pilot's license, juggling flying with band and swim-team practice. By 21, he was a flight instructor, teaching a new crop of budding aviators.

His youthful appearance would often make his students do a double take, said Allen, who now, at 25, has 1,800 hours of flying experience and is aiming for a job at a regional airline. "They'd look at me and are like, 'You're my flight instructor?'" he recalled.

Pilots both young and old say they could relate to Nathalia Filgueiras — the 20-year-old co-pilot at the radio in the harrowing seconds before a Learjet crashed into a Florida neighborhood on Sunday. Her dedication to flying in her teens wasn't an anomaly, but part of a growing wave of young people getting an early start in their pilot careers.

Like Filgueiras, many are getting in the cockpit before finishing high school.

"You don't build those years of experience by doing nothing," said Allen, who caught the aviation bug as a child growing up near the airport in Galesburg, Ill.

At 17, Filgueiras already had her private pilot's license. "Some people think that it's, like, weird because I can fly planes, but I can't drive a car," the then-high-schooler in Boca Raton, Fla., told a local CBS News affiliate back in 2023. On Instagram, her former flight instructor called her "without a doubt the most naturally gifted pilot I have ever taught."

Investigators are currently looking into the specifics of the crash — which killed Filgueiras and eight others on board — and it isn't clear who was piloting the aircraft at the time. Typically, though, the person on the radio wouldn't be in control of the plane, aviation experts say. Audio shows Filgueiras stayed on the radio and relayed what was happening during the rapid descent.

"That is just unbelievable control," says Karen Kalishek, chair of the National Association of Flight Instructors.

More teenagers have pursued pilot certificates over the past decade, drawn in part by an industry push to attract more young adults into the field. In 2025, the Federal Aviation Administration estimated that 914 people ages 16 to 19 held commercial flight certificates, up from 693 the year before. (Commercial certificates don't expire, so people can remain in the same age category the following year.)

The industry stepped up its outreach to schools and scholarship programs amid a postpandemic shortage of commercial-airline pilots. Though the shortage has abated, the industry is expected to need to replace thousands more pilots each year.

"We see a lot of retirements coming, and the airlines are growing," said Katie Pribyl, acting co-president of the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association. Pribyl herself was flying at 18 in the late 1990s, and by 21, she was working for an airline.

Almost always, there is a wait list when high schools adopt AOPA's nearly decade-old aviation curriculum, she says. More than 34,000 students are enrolled in the courses this school year across more than 1,700 high schools.

Rancho High School in Las Vegas admits 60 students to its flight program each year. The teenagers spend the first two years preparing to take the FAA's written exam, and, by 11th grade, or age 16, log hours in an aircraft. Rancho already has two juniors who have flown solo, says Ryan Ruttan, who coordinates the school's magnet programs.

"Most of us don't know what we wanna do at 16, 17, 18," he says. "They're mature beyond their years."

Emma Mitchell, a 21-year-old pilot who got her start at 18, said she didn't know at first what she wanted to do after high school — except avoid an office cubicle. She googled "jobs that aren't 9-to-5s," and aviation popped up. After an introductory flight lesson, she was all-in.

While she studied for an associate degree for business administration — a fallback plan, she says — Mitchell balanced working 25 hours a week with one day of flying. She then committed to a full-time, accelerated flight-school program and graduated at 20 with a commercial pilot's license. She now works as a flight instructor to accrue enough hours to apply to an airline.

To earn a private certificate, pilots must be at least 17 and have at least 40 hours of flight experience, including 10 hours solo. Pilots must be 18 and have 250 hours of flight time to earn a commercial certificate, though that doesn't mean they can fly for a major airline.

Getting that certification requires being at least 23 years old and having 1,500 hours of flying experience. (Military pilots and those who graduate from an aviation college or university program can obtain a restricted license at 21 with fewer flying hours.) At each level of the certification process, the expectations increase and every person — no matter the age — meets the same standards.

"It's not handed on a silver platter," said Kalishek, of the flight instructor organization. "They have to pass rigorous evaluations."

Flying charter flights — like the one Filgueiras was co-piloting — is one way pilots build up the hours of experience they need to make the jump to an airline. New pilots learn not only through their formal training but also by soaking up the knowledge imparted in the cockpit by the more experienced captains they fly with.

"It works out really well. You're usually flying next to somebody that has an extensive amount of experience," says Bob Allen, 60, a former airline pilot (and no relation to Parker Allen) who now runs a business ferrying jets around the world for airlines and lessors. He started flying as a 16-year-old in Lexington, Ky.

This week he took to social media to hail Filgueiras and the expertise she developed in her cut-short career.

"Many of us were that 18 or 20 year old co-pilot a long time ago," he posted on X. "And we were good at what we did as I'm certain she was, too."

Write to Allison Pohle at allison.pohle@wsj.com and Alison Sider at alison.sider@wsj.com

With CHALET’s operational hotels’ portfolio poised to grow by 1,655 keys to over 5,400 keys by Mar’30E, alongside its leasing traction, we estimate 15%/20% revenue/EBITDA CAGRs over FY26–29 (ex-residential). Retain BUY with an unchanged SoTPbased TP of INR 1,095, basis 22x Mar’28E hotel EV/EBITDA. Key risks: Slowdown in hotel demand and office leasing.

Outlook

We retain BUY with an unchanged SoTP-based TP of INR 1,095, based on 22x Mar’28E hotel EV/EBITDA, 8% cap rate for rental assets, and residual value of Vivarea, Bengaluru residential project.

data.title: IRCTC intensifies crackdown on unauthorised E-catering platforms to safeguard Railway passengers
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) has launched a stringent enforcement drive to identify and curb the operations of unauthorised e-catering websites and mobile applications operating across the Indian Railways network.

According to IRCTC, the proliferation of unauthorised e-catering platforms poses serious risks to passenger food safety, hygiene and overall well-being. IRCTC added that such platforms often source meals from unlicensed food outlets that may not comply with the prescribed Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regulations and hygiene standards.

It further claimed that these outlets may operate in unhygienic conditions, employ untrained food handlers and deploy delivery personnel without the mandatory medical examinations, thereby compromising food quality and passenger safety.

In addition to health and hygiene concerns, these unauthorised platforms expose passengers to significant risks relating to data privacy, financial security and consumer protection.

Sharing sensitive information, including Passenger Name Record (PNR) details, email addresses, mobile numbers and payment credentials through unverified platforms can leave passengers vulnerable to phishing attacks, identity misuse and financial fraud.

Passengers also face the risk of orders being cancelled, delayed or never delivered, often without any effective customer support or grievance-redressal mechanism. In the absence of a formal complaint-handling system, affected passengers may find it difficult to recover their money or pursue appropriate legal remedies.

Recognising the importance of protecting passengers' health, safety, privacy and financial interests, IRCTC took action against entities unlawfully operating e-catering services or misusing the IRCTC brand and identity to conduct unauthorised business.

The Corporation has intensified enforcement measures and moved beyond issuing warnings to initiating stringent legal action against non-compliant entities involved in unauthorised food delivery operations and related violations.

IRCTC advised passengers to book their meals during train journeys exclusively through the official website, official Food on Track mobile application, or IRCTC-authorised e-catering aggregators and vendors

The updated list of authorised e-catering partners is available on the official IRCTC e-Catering website and mobile application.

Passengers who encounter unauthorised food vendors or illegal food delivery activities on railway premises or trains are encouraged to report such incidents to the Railway Protection Force (RPF) by calling its helpline number 182.

According to IRCTC, the operations of unauthorised e-catering networks have significant financial and regulatory implications. While IRCTC contributes GST on its e-catering revenue, unauthorised operators functioning outside the prescribed regulatory framework may evade applicable statutory tax obligations. Such activities not only undermine fair competition and regulatory compliance but also potentially result in substantial losses to the public exchequer.

Through its e-Catering platform, IRCTC has established a standard for passenger convenience, choice and accessibility, transforming the way passengers enjoy meals during train journeys.

One of the platform's key strengths is the wide variety of food choices available to passengers. From regional delicacies and traditional Indian meals to popular fast-food options such as pizza, burgers, etc., the platform caters to diverse tastes and preferences. Passengers can also order cakes and other special food items to celebrate occasions such as birthdays and anniversaries while travelling, said IRCTC.

The IRCTC further added that meal prices are market-driven, with individual restaurant partners curating their own menus and pricing. This flexible model offers passengers the freedom to select meals according to their preferences, budgets and special requirements, ensuring a convenient and personalised dining experience throughout their journey

IRCTC remains committed to ensuring safe, hygienic, reliable and secure catering services for railway passengers. Passengers are advised to place food orders only through IRCTC's officially authorised e-catering channels to protect themselves from potential health, financial and data-security risks, said release.
